name: Wasmer

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Includes the same 6 active CPU-hours, 400 GB-hours RAM, 150 GB bandwidth, 1 GB volume/package storage, 1M requests and 1,000 build minutes as Hobby; overages $0.10/CPU-h, $0.01/GB-h RAM, $0.10/GB egress, $0.05/GB storage, $0.50/M requests, $0.005/build-min, $0.25/app after 100, $0.01/domain after 50, $0.001/email; database $0.01/MB; one daily backup then $0.20/backup.

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: Free forever; 1 member, 100 apps, 500 deploys/month, 1M requests, 150 GB bandwidth, 6 active CPU-hours, 400 GB-hours memory, 1 GB volume and package storage, 100 MB database per app, 1,000 build minutes, 50 custom domains; low execution priority; no SSH/SFTP.

caveats: Wasmer WebAssembly execution is not a full Linux VM; card isolation isolate is approximate because engine lacks wasm enum. Pricing uses active CPU plus provisioned memory.

Pro includes separate 6 active CPU-hours, 400 GB-hours memory, 150 GB bandwidth, 1 GB volume and package storage, 1M requests and 1000 build-minutes. These category-specific allowances cannot be collapsed into fully fungible credits.
Pro $10/mo; extra seats $5, app beyond 100 $0.25, requests $0.50/M, builds $0.005/min, volumes/packages $0.05/GB-month; databases and backups separate.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: one of the features on our roadmap is persistent instances, which will keep running, and won't be dynamically spawned or terminated
snapshot_auto.note: Instances are ephemeral (terminated after a few idle minutes or evicted); nothing saves an instance's state at stop. InstaBoot is automatic but different: Edge warms up a fresh instance, snapshots it (journal+memory) per app version and boots new instances from that snapshot; it does not carry a stopped instance's state forward. Durable state only via volumes/databases.

guest_firewall.note: Workloads are WebAssembly/WASIX instances on the Wasmer runtime, not a Linux VM or container: there is no guest kernel netfilter, so nftables/iptables cannot run.

secret_proxy.quote: You can manage secure environment variables - from now on simply _secrets_ -
secret_proxy.note: App secrets are environment variables injected into the app (CLI wasmer app secrets create/list/reveal/update/delete, or dashboard); no injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Volumes provide persistent disk storage for applications.
volume_attach.note: Declared in app.yaml (name + mount path), multiple per app, single region only; also S3-API remote access and SFTP. $0.05/GB-month on pricing page.

volume_shared.quote: Keep in mind that volumes can be accessed concurrently, and even from different nodes.
volume_shared.note: Read-write-many ('volumes at the moment only provide *read-write-many* semantics'); all auto-scaled instances of an app share them, including across nodes in the one region. Not recommended for single-writer databases.
